record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: For metric spaces X and Y, let A_e(X,Y) be the set of all α in (0,1] such that every (K,α)-Hölder map from a subset of X into Y admits, for every C > 1, an extension to all of X that is (CK,α)-Hölder. Must A_e(X,Y) always be closed in (0,1]? If it is closed, must one also have A_e(X,Y) = A(X,Y), where A(X,Y) = B_1(X,Y) is the set of α for which isometric extension is possible?

evidence.quote: If C = 1, such an extension is called an isometric extension. When C > 1, it is called an isomorphic extension. If a (CK, α)-H¨older extension exists for all C > 1, we say that f can be almost isometrically extended. Thus the following sets are defined: A(X, Y ) = B1(X, Y ), B(X, Y ) = [ C≥1 BC(X, Y ), Ae(X, Y ) = \ C>1 BC(X, Y ).
Problem 5.1. Is Ae(X, Y ) always closed? If yes, is Ae(X, Y ) = A(X, Y )?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d_X)$ and $(Y,d_Y)$ be metric spaces. For constants $K>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1]$, a map $f:S\to Y$ defined on a subset $S\subseteq X$ is called $(K,\alpha)$-Hölder if
$$d_Y(f(x),f(x'))\le K\,d_X(x,x')^{\alpha}\quad\text{for all }x,x'\in S.$$
For $C\ge 1$, let $B_C(X,Y)$ denote the set of those $\alpha\in(0,1]$ such that every $(K,\alpha)$-Hölder map $f:S\to Y$, defined on any subset $S\subseteq X$, admits an extension $\tilde f:X\to Y$ which is $(CK,\alpha)$-Hölder. Define
$$A(X,Y)=B_1(X,Y),\qquad A_e(X,Y)=\bigcap_{C>1}B_C(X,Y).$$
Thus $\alpha\in A_e(X,Y)$ means every $(K,\alpha)$-Hölder map from a subset of $X$ into $Y$ admits, for every $C>1$, a $(CK,\alpha)$-Hölder extension to all of $X$ (an "almost isometric" extension), while $\alpha\in A(X,Y)$ means an isometric ($C=1$) extension always exists.

(a) Is the set $A_e(X,Y)$ always closed in $(0,1]$?

(b) Whenever $A_e(X,Y)$ is closed, must one have $A_e(X,Y)=A(X,Y)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches reveal related work on isometric vs. isomorphic Hölder extension (e.g., Naor's phase-transition results for Hölder maps between $L_p$ spaces, and results on extension into $C(K)$ spaces), but no source was found that explicitly resolves whether $A_e(X,Y)$ is always closed in $(0,1]$, nor whether closedness implies $A_e(X,Y)=A(X,Y)$. The status of this specific question could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: A phase transition phenomenon between the isometric and isomorphic extension problems for Hölder functions between Lp spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the gap between isometric and isomorphic (arbitrarily small loss) Hölder extension constants between Lp spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature studies the isometric vs. almost-isometric Hölder extension dichotomy but does not appear to resolve the closedness of A_e(X,Y) or its equality with A(X,Y) in general.

status_evidence.title: On the extension of Hölder maps with values in spaces of continuous functions
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes when α-Hölder maps from subsets of a Banach space into c_0 or C(K) admit isometric extensions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial results on the isometric extension set A(X,Y) for specific target spaces but does not address the general closedness question for A_e(X,Y).
